articles.title: Newscast - The Undercover Reform Donations Investigation - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Two senior Reform UK officials step down after undercover donations report.
articles.body: Today, two senior officials have stood down from Reform UK after a Channel 4 News report prompts the party to investigate claims about funding. Nigel Farage's senior aide Dan Jukes and Reform's head of policy James Orr have both stood down pending the outcome of the internal probe. The undercover filming was done by Verbatim Investigations and broadcast by Channel 4 News. Reform UK has denied wrongdoing and Nigel Farage describes the operation as entrapment. The footage appears to show an attempt to secure funding from someone they believed to be a foreign donor. Electoral law prohibits UK political parties from receiving financial contributions from people who can't vote here. Reform denies any wrongdoing and says it has "been the target of a hoax perpetuated by foreign-funded climate change activists". Adam and Chris discuss. This episode was recorded at 11.30am on Friday. You can now listen to Newscast on a smart speaker. If you want to listen, just say "Ask BBC Sounds to play Newscast”. It works on most smart speakers. You can join our Newscast online community here: Get in touch with Newscast by emailing newscast@bbc.co.uk or send us a WhatsApp on +44 0330 123 9480. New episodes released every day. If you're in the UK, for more News and Current Affairs podcasts from the BBC, listen on BBC Sounds: Newscast brings you daily analysis of the latest political news stories from the BBC. The presenter was Adam Fleming. It was made by Jack Maclaren with Miranda Slade and Nik Sindle. The social producers were Joe Wilkinson and Beth Pritchard. The technical producer was Mike Regaard. The assistant editor is Chris Gray. The senior news editor is Sam Bonham.

articles.title: 'We expect our sons to be killed,' father of teen shot dead in West Bank tells BBC
articles.summary: Palestinian teenagers Omar al-Naasan and Khalil Abu Alia were shot dead when Israeli settlers and soldiers entered a village in the occupied West Bank.
articles.body:
Funerals have taken place for two Palestinian teenagers who were shot dead this week when settlers and soldiers entered a Palestinian village in the occupied West Bank.

The killing of Omar al-Naasan and Khalil Abu Alia comes amid near-daily attacks by Jewish settlers in the village of al-Mughayyir, south of Nablus.

"We expect that when our sons walk in the street, they are likely to return to you injured or killed," Mohammed Al-Naasan, Omar's father, told the BBC.

articles.title: Governo não proibiu uso de estribos em caminhões de coleta de lixo | G1
articles.standfirst: Norma não proíbe o uso de plataformas operacionais, mas estabelece regras de utilização durante o deslocamento para garantir a segurança dos trabalhadores.
articles.summary: Norma não proíbe o uso de plataformas operacionais, mas estabelece regras de utilização durante o deslocamento para garantir a segurança dos trabalhadores.
articles.body:
É #FAKE que norma do governo proíbe uso de estribos em caminhões de coleta de lixo — Foto: Reprodução

Circulam nas redes sociais publicações alegando que uma nova norma do Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) teria proibido o uso de estribos em caminhões de coleta de lixo. É #FAKE .

Publicados ao menos desde 31 de agosto no TikTok , Facebook e Instagram , os posts alegam que o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego teria proibido o uso de estribos (plataformas localizadas na parte traseira de caminhões), mencionando que a regra foi alterada pela Norma Regulamentadora n°38 (NR-38).

Uma das publicações exibe duas imagens de caminhões de lixo e de coletores apoiados em cima das plataformas. O texto acima das fotos diz: "Ministério do Trabalho proíbe estribo em caminhões de coleta de lixo, usado para garis descansar. Agora os trabalhadores terão que correr todo percurso" .

A legenda do post alega: "O Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego endureceu as regras de segurança para profissionais da limpeza urbana por meio da NR-38 [...]" .

Mas isso não é verdade. A NR-38 foi aprovada em dezembro de 2022, ainda durante o governo do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL). Além disso, a norma não proíbe o uso de estribos (plataformas operacionais), mas estabelece regras de utilização durante o deslocamento para garantir a segurança dos trabalhadores - leia mais abaixo .

Procurado pelo Fato ou Fake , o Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego informou que "não há proibição de uso de estribo durante o trabalho de coleta" e enviou um comunicado oficial, publicado no site da pasta nesta quarta-feira (2).

Segundo a nota, a Norma Regulamentadora n°38 (NR-38) foi aprovada em 16 de dezembro de 2022 , e passou a valer a partir de 2 de janeiro de 2024.

Ela estabelece regras de segurança e medidas de bem-estar para as atividades de limpeza urbana e manejo de resíduos sólidos, como fornecimento de equipamentos de proteção e água potável durante o serviço.

➡️ A NR-38 também determina condições para o uso dos estribos dos caminhões durante a coleta . Veja as regras de utilização:

os trabalhadores podem subir e descer da plataforma somente quando o veículo estiver totalmente parado;

a velocidade do caminhão deve ser limitada a 10 km/h durante a coleta;

antes de movimentar o veículo, o motorista deve aguardar o sinal sonoro dos coletores;

os coletores não podem permanecer na plataforma enquanto a marcha à ré estiver acionada ou durante o processo de compactação.

➡️ O que a NR-38 realmente proíbe? A plataforma não pode ser utilizada como meio de transporte quando o caminhão deixa de realizar a coleta e se desloca . Isso inclui trajetos como:

ida e volta entre áreas de coleta e empresa;

até locais de transbordo e de destinação final dos resíduos;

entre setores de coleta que não sejam adjacentes (vizinhos).

Portanto, se houver continuidade na coleta entre áreas vizinhas, o uso é permitido. Nas circunstâncias mencionadas, os trabalhadores devem estar em um veículo legalmente habilitado e em devidas condições.

O Fato ou Fake também consultou o Sindicato dos Trabalhadores e Trabalhadoras em Empresas de Prestação de Serviços de Asseio e Conservação e Limpeza Urbana de São Paulo (Siemaco-SP). Em nota, o sindicato também desmentiu as alegações:

"O SIEMACO São Paulo esclarece que não houve qualquer alteração na Norma Regulamentadora nº 38 (NR-38) que determine a retirada do estribo (denominado plataforma operacional na norma) utilizado pelos trabalhadores da coleta de resíduos sólidos urbanos".

Segundo o sindicato, a manutenção do uso de estribo foi uma decisão com participação direta da categoria, por meio de assembleia, e só pode ser alterada se houver discussão entre trabalhadores, empregadores e governo federal.

A nota também afirma que: "A NR-38 é conquista dos trabalhadores da limpeza urbana e será defendida com a responsabilidade que o tema exige. O SIEMACO-SP permanecerá vigilante para que informações infundadas não retirem a tranquilidade de milhares de profissionais que, diariamente, prestam serviço essencial à população".

articles.title: David Almeida Eleições 2026: Propostas para pequenos negócios no AM | G1
articles.standfirst: Durante a caminhada, o candidato do Avante afirmou que pretende levar para os municípios do interior ações voltadas aos pequenos negócios que, segundo ele, foram implantadas durante a gestão na Prefeitura de Manaus.
articles.summary: David Almeida apresentou o projeto Empreende Amazonas para fortalecer pequenos negócios e feiras em todo o estado durante caminhada em Manaus.
articles.body:
David Almeida participa de caminhada em Manaus e apresenta propostas para pequenos negócios Foto — Foto: Jadson Lima/g1 AM

O candidato ao governo do Amazonas, David Almeida ( Avante ), participou de uma caminhada de campanha no bairro da Paz, em Manaus , na manhã desta sexta-feira (4). Ao lado de candidatos a deputados estaduais e federais, ele conversou com moradores e feirantes e apresentou propostas para mercados, feiras e pequenos empreendedores.

David Almeida disputa o cargo pela coligação "Pra Cima, Amazonas", formada pelo Avante, Solidariedade, PRD, PDT, Democracia Cristã (DC) e Agir. O candidato é ex-prefeito de Manaus, cumpriu três mandatos consecutivos como deputado estadual e assumiu interinamente o Governo do Amazonas por três meses em 2017.

Durante a caminhada, o candidato afirmou que pretende levar para os municípios do interior ações voltadas aos pequenos negócios que, segundo ele, foram implantadas durante a gestão na Prefeitura de Manaus.

"Nós temos o Empreende Amazonas, onde a nossa proposta para levar o que nós fizemos em Manaus com os mercados e feiras, os pequenos negócios, levar também para todo o estado do Amazonas, melhorando então o ambiente de negócio e aumentando o faturamento desses micro e pequenos empreendedores", disse.

David Almeida também afirmou que pretende levar aos municípios do interior projetos realizados durante sua gestão na capital. Segundo ele, a campanha deve incluir visitas a diferentes cidades do estado.

Após a caminhada, o candidato deve gravar o programa eleitoral às 11h. À tarde, segundo a campanha, ele participa de outra caminhada, desta vez no bairro Alvorada, em Manaus. A agenda pode sofrer alterações.

A campanha eleitoral começou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Os candidatos já podem fazer propaganda nas ruas e na internet. Na TV e no rádio, a propaganda começou no dia 28 de agosto. O primeiro turno das eleições será no dia 4 de outubro.

articles.title: Curta produzido por jovens indígenas do AC é exibido em mostra on-line | G1
articles.standfirst: Curta-metragem foi gravado entre maio e junho na Aldeia Puyanawa, em Mâncio Lima, e nasceu de curso on-line voltado a jovens de comunidades tradicionais da Amazônia. Exibição ocorre nesta sexta (4).
articles.summary: Filme foi gravado entre maio e junho na Aldeia Puyanawa, em Mâncio Lima, e nasceu de curso on-line voltado a jovens de comunidades tradicionais da Amazônia.
articles.body:
Relação de mulheres Puyanawa com ancestralidade é tema de curta-metragem gravado em Mâncio Lima — Foto: Divulgação

A relação das mulheres Puyanawa com a ancestralidade e com um espaço sagrado do território indígena é o tema de um curta-metragem produzido por três jovens da Aldeia Puyanawa, em Mâncio Lima , no interior do Acre, que é exibido em uma mostra on-line e gratuita nesta sexta-feira (4) , às 17h (horário local).

O filme 'O desafio das mulheres Puyanawa para chegar até a maloca sagrada' integra produções audiovisuais feitas por jovens de comunidades tradicionais da Amazônia, foi produzido por Carol Puyanawa, Sara Januário e Rair Puyanawa e gravado entre maio e junho.

Segundo a organização do evento, a produção acreana apresenta, a partir do relato de Maria Valéria (Xinã Iruya), a relação das mulheres Puyanawa com a maloca sagrada e com os conhecimentos transmitidos entre gerações, a partir do olhar de quem vive no próprio território.

A produção surgiu a partir de um curso on-line de audiovisual realizado pela Rede Comunitária Floresta Digital, que ofereceu aos participantes formação em narrativa, produção, captação de imagens e edição de vídeos.

"Cada participante de cada território integrante da rede utilizou os recursos que tinham a disposição para construir uma narrativa em audiovisual que falasse ou representasse sua cultura, identidade e comunidade", complementou.

O curta Puyanawa integra o Cine Floresta Digital, mostra virtual que reúne três filmes produzidos durante a formação audiovisual da Rede. Além do Acre, participam produções do Amapá e do Pará:

No Amapá , o filme 'Empreendedores do Açaí', produzido por Rafael Brutti Eckhardt, da Associação Nossa Amazônia, mostra experiências de jovens da Escola Família Agroextrativista do Carvão, em Mazagão, relacionadas à produção e ao empreendedorismo em torno do açaí.

Já o Pará participa com 'Contos e Lendas de Acará-Açu', de Ingrid Beatriz, da comunidade Acará-Açu. A produção reúne histórias de visagens e assombrações que fazem parte da memória e da tradição local.

A exibição também conta com comentários e devolutivas da jornalista e documentarista Tainá Barral, da Associação Cultural Na Cuia, em uma conversa sobre os processos de produção e as narrativas construídas pelos jovens realizadores.

Curtas são produzidos por jovens indígenas de três estados — Foto: Divulgação

Ao final da programação, os participantes que concluíram os filmes devem receber acessórios para celular, que poderão ser utilizados em novas produções audiovisuais dentro dos próprios territórios.

O Cine Floresta Digital faz parte das ações da Rede Comunitária Floresta Digital, iniciativa desenvolvida pelo Projeto Saúde e Alegria e pela DW Akademie, com apoio da União Europeia. A rede atua em nove territórios indígenas, ribeirinhos e quilombolas dos estados do Pará, Acre, Amapá e Amazonas.

O projeto combina a implantação de infraestruturas comunitárias de internet com formações voltadas a jovens e lideranças em áreas como cultura digital, comunicação e gestão tecnológica.

Filmes foram gravados com celulares e editados a partir de oficinas on-line — Foto: Divulgação

articles.title: Influenciadores do tigrinho são denunciados à Justiça por esquema que movimentou R$ 67,5 milhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Foram denunciados Adrielly Vivianny Araújo de Jesus, Dione dos Santos da Silva, Raniely Silva Carvalho, Patrik Adhan dos Santos Ribeiro, Amanda Lourenço Faria, Laís Ramos Gomes da Silva, Victoria Paixão Barros, Vitória Reis da Silva, Juliana Lima do Nascimento e Gildázio Sobrinho Santos Cardoso.
articles.summary: Foram denunciados Adrielly Vivianny Araújo de Jesus, Dione dos Santos da Silva, Raniely Silva Carvalho, Patrik Adhan dos Santos Ribeiro, Amanda Lourenço Faria, Laís Ramos Gomes da Silva, Victoria Paixão Barros, Vitória Reis da Silva, Juliana Lima do Nascimento e Gildázio Sobrinho Santos Cardoso.
articles.body:
Investigados por esquema de jogos de azar: Adrielly Vivianny Araújo de Jesus e o marido Dione dos Santos da Silva, Raniely Silva Carvalho, Patrik Adhan dos Santos Ribeiro, Amanda Lourenço Faria, Laís Ramos Gomes da Silva, Victoria Paixão Barros, Vitória Reis da Silva, Juliana Lima do Nascimento e Gildázio Sobrinho Santos Cardoso. — Foto: Reprodução

Nove influenciadores digitais e um empresário foram denunciados à Justiça , nesta sexta-feira (4), por integrarem um esquema de divulgação de plataformas clandestinas de jogos de azar como o tigrinho , em Roraima. Juntos, eles receberam R$ 67,5 milhões em quase dois anos, segundo o Ministério Público do estado. Os denunciados são :

Adrielly Vivianny Araújo de Jesus — influenciadora

Dione dos Santos da Silva — empresário, marido de Adrielly

Patrik Adhan dos Santos Ribeiro — influenciadora

Laís Ramos Gomes da Silva — influenciadora

Juliana Lima do Nascimento — influenciadora

Gildázio Sobrinho Santos Cardoso — influenciadora

Eles foram denunciados pelos crimes de exploração de jogos de azar , afirmação falsa ou enganosa sobre produtos ou serviços , indução do consumidor a erro , crimes contra a economia popular, associação criminosa e lavagem de dinheiro . Três deles também foram denunciados por estelionato .

Em nota, a defesa de Raniely disse que "as acusações não correspondem à realidade". Já a defesa dos investigados Adrielly , Dione e Patrick informou que "se pronunciará nos autos e não adiantará qualquer estratégia técnica", enquanto a de Gildázio negou os crimes atribuídos a ele e disse que "confia que terá assegurados o contraditório" (leia as notas na íntegra abaixo) .

A defesa das investigadas Victoria e Vitória também foi procurada, mas não enviou resposta até a última atualização. A reportagem tenta localizar os demais.

Segundo o MP, o esquema fraudulento funcionava por meio da divulgação de plataformas clandestinas de jogos de azar nas redes sociais.

Os influenciadores publicavam stories, reels e vídeos com links personalizados e exibiam supostos ganhos , veículos, imóveis, viagens e outros bens para atrair seguidores com a promessa de lucro fácil.

Os seguidores eram direcionados às plataformas para realizar cadastros e depósitos, enquanto os divulgadores recebiam comissões pela captação de novos apostadores. Além disso, usavam contas de demonstração fornecidas pelas plataformas para simular ganhos expressivos e irreais.

Após os depósitos, os usuários visualizavam supostos lucros e eram incentivados a continuar apostando . Ao tentar sacar quantias maiores, no entanto, enfrentavam bloqueios ou negativas para a retirada dos valores.

A associação criminosa era estruturada em três núcleos interligados :

Operacional e Empresarial reunia responsáveis pela administração das plataformas clandestinas, operadores financeiros e intermediadoras de pagamento;

Núcleo de Divulgação e Captação , integrado pelos influenciadores, atuava na divulgação dos jogos e na atração de apostadores;

Núcleo de Ocultação Financeira seria responsável por ocultar e dissimular a origem e a propriedade dos recursos obtidos com o esquema.

O promotor de Justiça autor da denúncia, Carlos Alberto Melotto, explica que a lavagem de dinheiro ocorria por meio da movimentação dos recursos em diferentes instituições financeiras, contas pessoais e jurídicas, além de transferências entre os denunciados e terceiros.

Os valores conseguidos com as plataformas também eram incorporados ao patrimônio por meio da aquisição de veículos, imóveis, viagens, procedimentos estéticos e outros bens de alto valor.

"Estamos falando de um esquema que explora a confiança das pessoas e a expectativa de obter ganhos financeiros, causando prejuízos que podem comprometer a renda e o patrimônio das vítimas. A atuação do Ministério Público busca interromper esse ciclo, responsabilizar os envolvidos e impedir que estruturas como essa continuem utilizando as redes sociais para alcançar novos consumidores”, destacou.

Na denúncia, feita pela Promotoria de Justiça Especializada em Organização Criminosa e Lavagem de Capitais, o MP pediu que três vítimas sejam indenizadas.

"A defesa, após analisar os elementos disponíveis, sustenta que as acusações não correspondem à realidade dos fatos e demonstrará, no momento processual adequado, a ausência de responsabilidade penal de Raniely Carvalho.

Por estratégia processual, não serão antecipados neste momento detalhes da manifestação defensiva."

"A defesa se pronunciará nos autos e não adiantará qualquer estratégia técnica".

"A defesa de GILDAZIO Cardoso informa que não fará comentários conclusivos sobre acusações apresentadas pelo MP que deverão ser devidamente apuradas no curso do processo.

GILDAZIO nega a prática dos crimes atribuídos a ele e confia que terá assegurados o contraditório, a ampla defesa e o devido processo legal.

Ressalta-se que o oferecimento de denúncia não implica condenação, permanecendo vigente a presunção de inocência até decisão judicial definitiva.

A defesa permanece à disposição para prestar esclarecimentos adicionais após o recebimento da denúncia."

articles.title: Rodovias da região de Piracicaba esperam 378 mil veículos no feriado | G1

articles.summary: Movimentação deve começar nesta sexta-feira (4) e segue até terça (8). Rodoviárias de Limeira e Piracicaba também registram aumento do movimento de passageiros.
articles.body:
Rodovia administrada pela concessionária Eixo SP — Foto: Divulgação/EIXOSP

As principais rodovias que cortam a região de Piracicaba (SP) devem ter fluxo de 378 mil veículos durante o feriado nacional da Independência do Brasil, celebrado nesta segunda-feira (7). A movimentação começa nesta sexta (4) e segue até a terça-feira (8).

A concessionária Eixo SP, responsável pelas rodovias Geraldo de Barros (SP-304), Hermínio Petrin (SP-308), Irineu Penteado (SP-191) e Washington Luís (SP-310), espera receber 163 mil veículos entre a tarde de sexta-feira (4) e a manhã de terça-feira (8).

O número corresponde a um aumento de cerca de 28% em comparação com o fluxo de veículos em dias normais.

articles.title: Eleições dos EUA começam com disputa sobre voto pelo correio | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeiras cédulas são enviadas na Carolina do Norte, enquanto governo e oposição travam batalha sobre as regras da votação.
articles.summary: Primeiras cédulas são enviadas na Carolina do Norte, enquanto governo e oposição travam batalha sobre as regras da votação.
articles.body:
Funcionários do Conselho Eleitoral do Condado de Wake preparam cédulas de voto por ausência, com instruções para votação, para serem enviadas pelo correio — Foto: Matt Ramey / AP

As eleições de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos começaram nesta sexta-feira (4), com o envio das primeiras cédulas pelo correio na Carolina do Norte, no leste do país. O início da votação ocorre em meio à disputa sobre as regras para o voto à distância .

O governo de Donald Trump , que tenta manter o controle do Congresso, voltou a pedir nesta semana que a Suprema Corte autorize, em caráter de urgência, a adoção de regras mais rígidas para o voto pelo correio enviado pelo Serviço Postal dos EUA.

Democratas acusam o governo republicano de criar dificuldades para os eleitores com as novas exigências. Entre as medidas está a ampliação do uso de códigos de barras nos envelopes das cédulas.

A Suprema Corte autorizou parcialmente mudanças nas regras do voto pelo correio . Uma juíza federal, no entanto, voltou a bloquear as medidas por considerar que não há tempo suficiente para colocá-las em prática antes da eleição.

A votação presencial está marcada para 3 de novembro em todo o país.

Os americanos vão escolher os ocupantes dos 435 assentos da Câmara dos Representantes e de cerca de um terço das cadeiras do Senado. Pesquisas apontam uma alta probabilidade de que os democratas retomem o controle da Câmara.

As eleições são marcadas pela inflação e pela guerra no Irã . O resultado vai definir quanto espaço Trump terá para avançar com sua agenda nos dois últimos anos de seu mandato.

A disputa pelo Senado deve ser mais apertada. Os republicanos têm atualmente 53 das 100 cadeiras, contra 47 dos democratas. Para assumir o controle da Casa, os democratas precisam conquistar pelo menos quatro cadeiras a mais do que os republicanos.

A empresa Decision Desk HQ projetou a possibilidade de um Senado dividido igualmente, com 50 cadeiras para cada partido. Nesse cenário, o vice-presidente republicano, JD Vance, teria o voto de desempate.

Republicanos e democratas tratam a eleição como um referendo sobre o governo Trump. A aprovação do presidente está no nível mais baixo de seu mandato : seis em cada dez americanos dizem desaprovar sua gestão.

Eleições de meio de mandato costumam representar uma derrota para o partido do presidente. Agora, a disputa é para saber qual será o tamanho do revés para Trump nas urnas.

articles.title: Vídeo: jacaré é flagrado predando sucuri no Pantanal de MT  | G1
articles.standfirst: Registro foi feito pelo guia de turismo Paulo Boute, que atua há mais de 40 anos na região e afirmou que, mesmo com décadas de experiência, ficou surpreso com a cena.
articles.summary: Registro foi feito pelo guia de turismo Paulo Boute, que atua há mais de 40 anos na região e afirmou que, mesmo com décadas de experiência, ficou surpreso com a cena.
articles.body:
Um jacaré foi flagrado atacando uma sucuri no Pantanal mato-grossense, na região de Porto Jofre, em Poconé (MT), nessa terça-feira (1º).

O registro foi feito pelo guia de turismo Paulo Boute, que atua há mais de 40 anos na região e já realizou mais de mil expedições pelo Pantanal.

Nas imagens, o jacaré aparece com a serpente presa à boca. O animal permanece imóvel por alguns instantes, enquanto a sucuri se movimenta e tenta se desvencilhar do predador.

Ao g1 , Paulo afirmou que, mesmo com décadas de experiência em campo, ficou surpreso com a cena.

“Quando fazemos um passeio na natureza, eu comparo com uma pescaria. Quando jogamos o anzol, não conseguimos predizer o que irá acontecer. Nada está em gaiola ou jaula, então acabamos sempre nos surpreendendo”, disse em entrevista ao g1.

Jacaré abocanha sucuri no Pantanal — Foto: Paulo Boute

Boute mudou-se para Mato Grosso aos 17 anos e começou a trabalhar como guia turístico no Pantanal. Ao longo de mais de quatro décadas de atividade, acumulou experiência em campo e participou de mais de mil expedições pela região.

Segundo ele, o jacaré não matou a sucuri imediatamente após o ataque, mas posteriormente conseguiu predá-la.

articles.title: Trisal formado por rainha de rodeio, irmã e agricultor repercute na imprensa internacional | G1
articles.body:
Rainha de rodeio revela que é casada com o mesmo homem que a irmã gêmea: 'Somos um trisal' — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Maicon Rueda

A história do trisal formado pela rainho do rodeio de Montividiu , Lara Alves, de 35 anos, a irmã gêmea dela, Laila Alves, e o agricultor Maycon Rueda, de 43, ganhou repercussão internacional. Isso aconteceu após a história da família ser publicada no portal de notícias europeu The Sun e no uruguaio Montevideo Portal.

O site europeu fez a postagem na quinta-feira (3). Com entrevistas concedidas ao g1 pelas irmãs, os portais contaram a história de como o trisal se conheceu, também dando detalhes sobre a dinâmica do relacionamento entre eles.

Nos comentários da publicação do The Sun, europeus reagiram positivamente a notícia. "O que quer que os faça felizes e, o mais importante, que proporcione aos filhos um ambiente seguro e estável", desejou um.

No portal uruguaio, internautas brincaram sobre o relacionamento. "Um sujeito muito esperto: tem duas mulheres, mas uma sogra só", comentou outro.

O caso repercutiu após o vídeo de uma entrevista de Lara logo após vencer o título de rainha do rodeio, em que ela contou que vive em um trisal com a irmã gêmea e o agricultor.

Os três dividem uma casa de dois andares em Montividiu e organizaram a convivência de forma dividida: Laila fica no piso superior, enquanto Lara ocupa a parte de baixo por preferência pessoal, próxima à cozinha.

Maycon explicou ao g1 que alterna as noites entre os dois pavimentos da casa para estar individualmente com cada companheira, pontuando que as irmãs não mantêm relacionamento íntimo entre si, mas compartilham uma forte ligação fraterna e de cumplicidade.

Juntos há 6 anos, Lara e Maycon namoraram durante dois anos no passado e ficaram separados por quatro anos, período em que ele começou o relacionamento com Laila. Após esse tempo, segundo Lara, os três decidiram formar a relação juntos.

Lara contou que, inicialmente, recusou a proposta da irmã de viver um relacionamento a três.

"Surgiu a proposta se eu ainda sentia alguma coisa por ele, e eu falei que sim. Aí ela [Laila]: 'Uai, vamos ficar nós três juntos?'. Minha irmã já é bem tranquila. De momento, eu falei: 'Não, você tá doida. Isso não dá certo, não'. E aí foi tentando até que a gente aceitou”, disse.

Lara contou que, embora no início o trio percebesse olhares de estranhamento por parte de terceiros, o relacionamento não foi um problema para os familiares, que tiveram uma reação positiva sobre.

“No começo, éramos julgados apenas por olhares. Ninguém nunca chegou a falar nada diretamente, mas nós percebíamos. Por outro lado, desde o início, todos da família aceitaram muito bem a relação, tanto a família dele quanto a nossa”, disse.

Após o caso ganhar repercussão nas redes sociais, Laila contou que eles receberam críticas nas redes sociais sobre o relacionamento. “A gente divide o mesmo homem, só que não tem bagunça, não tem nada do que o povo pensa. Aonde a gente vai, a gente respeita todo mundo e todo mundo respeita a gente”, explicou.

Apesar das críticas, Maycon reforçou que as dúvidas sobre o cotidiano superam os julgamentos.

"O que eu mais escuto é curiosidade sobre como tudo funciona. Nunca imaginei ficar famoso por isso. Claro que tem críticas, mas é algo normal diante de um relacionamento fora do padrão", pontuou.

articles.title: Goiano diverte ao narrar decolagem de avião no aeroporto de Goiânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Vídeo foi gravado no estacionamento de uma transportadora, perto da BR-153, e acumula mais de 300 mil visualizações.
articles.summary: Vídeo foi gravado no estacionamento de uma transportadora, perto da BR-153, e acumula mais de 300 mil visualizações.
articles.body:
O goiano Odair Cardoso se divertiu ao narrar a decolagem de um avião no Aeroporto Santa Genoveva de Goiânia ( veja acima ). O vídeo foi gravado no estacionamento de uma transportadora, perto da BR-153. “O barulho é de uma carreta”, brincou.

O vídeo foi postado no final de julho e acumula mais de 300 mil visualizações nas redes sociais. Nas imagens, é possível ver um avião menor aterrissando na pista principal e outro maior aguardando para decolar.

“Aqui não tem prioridade quem é maior, quem é menor, não, meu amigo. Quem estiver no ar é que tem prioridade. O do chão já está no chão mesmo, que espere a sua vez”, explicou Odair na gravação.

Goiano diverte ao narrar decolagem de avião no aeroporto de Goiânia, Goiás — Foto: Reprodução/TikTok de Odair Cardoso

Ao g1 , Odair contou que é de Caldas Novas e trabalha com energia solar. No momento em que gravou o vídeo, ele estava em um treinamento perto do aeroporto de Goiânia. Ele revelou que gosta de ficar observando o movimento das aeronaves na pista, mas que viajou de avião apenas uma vez de Goiânia para São Paulo, em 2013.

“Vi que aquele pôr do sol estava bonito, admirando ali e comecei a gravar. Mas que bom que o pessoal está gostando. Eu acho que é meu jeito simples mesmo de observar as coisas, aí foi do que o pessoal gostou”, esclareceu.

Nos comentários do post, os seguidores admiraram a beleza da decolagem do avião e da paisagem do Aeroporto de Goiânia. “Eu trampo lá todos os dias, eu me surpreendo vendo esses aviões, é incrível”, disse um dos seguidores. “Linda subida com este pôr do sol maravilhoso demais e incrível”, declarou outra.

In a statement, he said he and his wife had faced "unimaginable heartache" and described it as "the most devastating time of our lives".

Howard praised the "extraordinary compassion, kindness and humanity" of the hospital staff who cared for them over the period that followed Felix's death.

He also announced the launch of a new foundation in their late son's name to help families going through similar ordeals, with a comedy fundraiser set to take place next year.

In a statement posted on his social media accounts on Friday, Howard recalled: "During our time in hospital, Felix was placed in a cool cot, which meant that my wife and I were able to spend precious hours with our beautiful boy.

He explained he and his wife had been assigned a bereavement midwife named Lauren, who had experienced a similar tragedy and retrained in order to help other families.

"Her care meant more to us than we could ever put into words," Howard said.

"We were overwhelmed by the care we received, and we made a promise to each other: that we would try to help other families who find themselves facing the same devastating circumstances."

As a result, Howard said he and Cerys were launching The Felix Foundation, which will aim to help families affected by miscarriage, premature birth, stillbirth, neonatal death or related bereavement.

articles.title: Man to stand trial for murder of police station janitor 27 years ago
articles.summary: Allan Humphrey, 68, allegedly killed Michael McManus, then 46, in the Riddrie area of Glasgow on 13 July 1999.
articles.body:
A man is to stand trial accused of the murder of a police station janitor in Glasgow more than 27 years ago.

Allan Humphrey, 68, allegedly killed Michael McManus on his way to work at Baird Street station in Riddrie on 13 July 1999.

Court papers state that Humphrey stabbed 46-year-old McManus on the body and leg with a knife or similar instrument.

Humphrey pleaded not guilty to the single charge of murder during a hearing at the High Court in Glasgow.

More stories from Glasgow & West Scotland

Donald Findlay KC, defending, lodged a special defence of incrimination against a named person, Michael Todd.

He said: "I discovered that Mr Todd is no longer with us as he died some years ago.

"It is a significant handicap for me during the trial.

"There is nothing I can do about it if he is dead, he is dead."

Prosecutor Alex Prentice KC also told the hearing there were further witnesses who have died since the incident.

McManus, who was also known as Mike, had worked as a janitor at the police station for three years at the time of his death.

BBC News reports from the time told how an attack took place as he was on his way to work.

McManus had been seen shouting into Ness Street before he was found dead by a passerby a short time later.

Checkpoints were set up after the incident by officers hoping to try to jog the memories of anyone in the Riddrie area.

The court heard that the trial would be down to eyewitnesses as there was no CCTV evidence.

An eight-day trial was fixed by Judge Lord Scott for the High Court in Edinburgh in November 2027.

articles.title: New robot lab in Liverpool to speed up disease research
articles.summary: Lab-grown human organs will be used to test treatments, reducing the need for animal testing.
articles.body:
Researchers in Liverpool say a new robotic laboratory could help speed up vaccine development and reduce the need for animal testing.

The £20m facility at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine will use lab-grown miniature human organs to test treatments for infectious diseases.

The facility, which has been supported by the Infection Innovation Consortium (iiCON), is due to be fully open by 2027.

Pro-vice chancellor for research and innovation, Prof Giancarlo Biagini, said: "It is really exciting to be involved and it's going to accelerate the way we develop drugs, vaccines and diagnostics."

Biagini said that the use of mini organs, such as the heart and brain, is "amazing technology", adding: "You can actually see the heart beating".

He said using tissue created from human donors, rather than animals, could improve research and provide more reliable data.

The school's former boss and founding member of iiCON, Prof Janet Hemingway, said the project will "create several hundred cutting-edge technology jobs".

She added: "Although the robots will do a lot of the work, we are training humans to develop that technology.

"Clinicians and researchers will be able to spend more of their time thinking how they do the science better rather than routine work."

articles.title: 'Not only did I survive, I thrived' - Meera Syal after assaults
articles.summary: The Wolverhampton-born comedian and actress shares her experiences in her new memoir.
articles.body:
Dame Meera Syal has said she "almost gave up" her career after being sexually harassed and assaulted by two "predators" within the media industry.

"I was out of work, I was homeless, sleeping on people's floors, and then these two things happened in quite quick succession," the Wolverhampton-born star said in a candid interview with BBC Asian Network's Amber Haque .

In her new memoir, Vigilauntie, which was published on Thursday, the actress shared that both incidents happened in her 20s, as she was struggling to secure a role.

Now aged 65, she has opened up about the harrowing experiences and reflected on how she overcame them to become one of the most well-known faces on British TV.

"It could have been a point where I gave up," she explained.

"It put some fire in my belly because the reason I wanted to tell these stories is that I did survive, and not only did I survive, I thrived.

"The anger of the injustice of the situation made me seek out a bunch of women that changed the course of my life."

Syal described the first incident as "my first casting couch approach".

She wrote that the man, a theatre director, insinuated he would give her a role in a pantomime if she engaged in sexual acts with him. She refused and was able to leave.

However, a few weeks later an older male actor invited her to his home under the guise that he would help her progress with her career. Instead he assaulted her, she wrote in her book.

The comedy star, known for shows including Goodness Gracious Me and The Kumars at No 42, did not report the incidents to the police and did not tell family or friends as it "was the culture" of the industry at the time.

She recalled: "When I have talked about this incident to other women, particularly of my age, they've all said that happened to me and a lot of them have never talked about it because it was part of the culture.

"The 70s, 80s and 90s, it was absolutely part of the culture.

"You wouldn't even bother to report half of these things because A, you wouldn't be believed and B, everyone was doing it."

Rather than turning away from the industry, Syal said she found strength and support in women's groups and began helping others.

The star added: "I got involved with Newham Asian Women's Project and Southall Black Sisters. I began campaigning because these issues became personal and I wanted to create South Asian women that roared.

"All of that came from the fury I felt at what had happened to me. It did change the course of my life."

Syal was born in Wolverhampton in 1961 to Indian Punjabi parents, who had moved to the UK from New Delhi. She later attended Queen Mary's High School in Walsall.

Last year, Syal was given a damehood in the King's New Year Honours for her services to literature, drama and charity.

Joining the BBC in the 1990s, she rose to prominence as part of the team behind the broadcaster's sketch comedy, Goodness Gracious Me!

In 1993, she wrote the screenplay for the comedy-drama film Bhaji On The Beach, and two years later she starred in the Channel 4 romantic comedy film, Beautiful Thing.

The award-winner was a key writer and actress on the 1996 show, and later helped to bring Bollywood to the West End, by co-writing Andrew Lloyd Webber's Bombay Dreams in 2002.

You can listen to the full interview with Dame Meera Syal on Asian Network Trending on BBC Sounds.

If you've been affected by the issues in this story, help and support is available via the BBC Action Line .

articles.title: US automakers urge Congress to ban sale of Chinese cars in America
articles.summary: US News: The Alliance for Automotive Innovation urges Congress to impose a permanent ban on Chinese vehicles in the US due to issues of competition and data security as Chinese automakers expand their market presence.
articles.body: A major US auto trade group is calling Congress to permanently ban Chinese vehicles in the country, warning that growing competition could threaten American auto production and raise data-security concerns.The Alliance for Automotive Innovation, which represents most automakers selling vehicles in the United States, requested in a letter to congressional leaders on Thursday. The group wants lawmakers to approve the restrictions before the current congressional session ends.Alliance president and CEO John Bozzella said Chinese companies benefit from government support while expanding into overseas markets.“Right now, Chinese automakers are dumping subsidized vehicles with connected software and hardware around the world,” Bozzella wrote in the letter.Chinese manufacturers, including BYD and Geely, have expanded exports to Europe, Australia, Southeast Asia, Mexico and countries across Central and South America. Their lower-priced vehicles have increased competition for established automakers and raised concerns about pressure on domestic manufacturing.Bozzella accused China of using industrial and manufacturing policies to disadvantage foreign competitors. He also cited alleged intellectual property theft and concerns that connected vehicles could collect and transmit sensitive information about vehicles and their users.“This behavior is a feature of the Chinese approach and especially acute when it comes to China’s strategy to dominate global automotive manufacturing and critical supply chains,” Bozzella wrote.Chinese automakers have made significant gains in electric vehicles. China is the world’s largest EV market and has become a major exporter as manufacturers seek growth outside the country.Bozzella said Chinese connected vehicles could gather consumer and vehicle data that might be accessible to Chinese authorities. He urged Congress to act before Chinese automakers establish a substantial presence in the US market.“This hasn’t happened inside the U.S. yet, but given the scale and urgency of this threat, we urge you to enact a Chinese vehicle, software and hardware ban before adjourning this year and make this policy the law of the land,” he wrote.The issue is already under consideration in Congress, where lawmakers from both parties are examining proposals to limit Chinese influence in the US automotive sector.Bozzella said a permanent ban approved by the current Congress would send a broader message about Washington’s response to China’s expansion in the global automotive industry.“Enacting a permanent ban on Chinese vehicles and high-risk hardware and software in the 119th Congress will send a clear and bipartisan message that China’s strategy to dominate global automotive manufacturing will be met with a national security policy response from the American government,” he wrote.The proposal comes as lawmakers face a crowded political calendar, including November’s midterm elections, which could affect the pace of action on China-related legislation.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Judge rules police statement can be used in fatal crash trial
articles.summary: Nathon Gibbon, 33, denies causing the deaths of three people in the Scottish Borders in July 2024.
articles.body:
A judge has ruled that a police statement given by a man accused of causing the deaths of three people in a motorbike crash can be used in evidence.

Nathon Gibbon, 33, is due to stand trial next year accused of causing the deaths of Jason Gibbon, Andrew Larty and Georgia Tate by driving a motorcycle dangerously in the Scottish Borders in July 2024.

It is alleged that he engaged in a "race or trial of speed" with the motorcycle driven by Jason Gibbon, exceeded the speed limit and continued to drive at "excessive speeds" as he approached a bend.

Nathon Gibbon, of Ashington, Northumberland, denies the charge and is due to stand trial in August next year.

Listen to news for the Scottish Borders on BBC Sounds

Prosecutors allege that Nathon Gibbon applied the brakes while Jason was in "close proximity" behind him, as a result of which Jason negotiated the bend at "excessive speeds" and entered the opposite carriageway where he collided with another motorcycle.

Andrew Larty, who was driving the other motorbike, his pillion passenger, Georgia Tate, both of Newcastle Upon Tyne, and Jason Gibbon, of Northumberland, were so severely injured that they died at the scene of the crash which happened on the A6088 between Bonchester Bridge and Carter Bar on 28 July 2024.

At a hearing at the High Court in Glasgow, Lord Macfadyen issued his decision following a hearing last month where lawyers representing Gibbon had called for his police statement not to be available as evidence.

The court heard that Gibbon, referred to as the "minuter", gave the statement to a police constable at a police station in the aftermath of the crash.

Lord Macfadyen said he was satisfied there was "no unfairness to the accused in the taking of the statement".

He said: "The police were investigating this tragic road traffic accident.

"The statement was made or started at a stage in that investigation before police suspicion had been placed on anybody.

"The minuter was not a suspect, there was no bullying or pressure."

He said it was clear that the police officer was treating Gibbon as a "witness not a suspect".

Lord Macfadyen ruled that the statement could be admissible in evidence.

Lily Prais KC, representing Gibbon, told the court that she would appeal against the judge's decision.

Gibbon was excused from attending the hearing.

articles.title: Isle of May puffin numbers plummet after extreme weather
articles.summary: Researchers said numbers in one of the UK's most significant colonies of the seabirds may have fallen by 30%.
articles.body:
Puffin numbers in one of the UK's largest colonies have suffered after a drop in food supplies and extreme weather conditions, conservationists have warned.

NatureScot said the number of burrows occupied by the seabirds on the Isle of May in the Firth of Forth had fallen by 30% in the last two years.

A joint survey also involving the UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology (UKCEH) suggested violent storms had killed a number of the birds, while rising ocean temperatures had seriously harmed populations of sand eels - their main source of food.

Researchers described the population decline as "disappointing and concerning".

About 36,500 burrows on the island – about 4.9 miles (8km) off the coast of Fife - were found to be in active use during the study carried out over the summer.

That marked a drop of nearly a third from the 52,000 burrows thought to be in use during the last survey of its kind in 2024.

Two puffins rescued after Storm Chandra return to wild

Puffins struggle to survive as Storm Chandra sweeps country

The Isle of May has been a national nature reserve (NNR) since 1956 and has been home to almost 300 species of birds.

The reserve's manager, David Steel, said the drop was reminiscent of the early 2000s, when puffin numbers fell before recovering in the 2010s.

"The decrease appears to be linked to a combination of ongoing pressures on seabird food supplies, poor winter survival and increasingly extreme weather conditions," he said.

"All of this underlines the importance of continued monitoring and conservation work at sites like the Isle of May NNR, where data and research are playing a vital role in helping us to understand these trends and respond."

The survey involved researchers sweeping back and forth across the island over a six-day period, counting burrows and assessing whether they were used by puffins or rabbits.

The island is also home to guillemots, fulmars, terns and gulls, thanks to its lack of predators.

In the autumn and winter months, it also plays host to thousands of breeding seals, while about 250 species of migrating birds use it as a stopover point.

Mark Newell, UKCEH's field manager on the Isle of May, said he was concerned future "extreme weather events" could affect the breeding ability of puffins and other species.

He said: "We believe that the puffin population has recently suffered from a series of extreme climate events, including marine heat waves and intense storms affecting survival in three of the last five winters.

"The concern for puffins and other seabirds is that climate scientists are predicting an increase in the frequency and severity of extreme events."

articles.title: Merthyr Tydfil football win over Atalanta made into theatre play
articles.summary: Merthyr Tydfil's first leg victory over Atalanta came while English sides were banned from European football.
articles.body:
Almost 40 years after Merthyr Tydfil FC stunned Italian footballing giants Atalanta in the European Cup Winners Cup, the remarkable story is being brought back to life on the theatre stage.

The comedy Just One Cornetto focuses on the weeks leading up to the match at the club's Penydarren Park, when Merthyr defeated the team from Bergamo 2-1, in the first round of the competition.

Disappointment was to follow with the thousands who had travelled from Merthyr to northern Italy having to suffer a 2-0 loss, which meant Atalanta would go through, eventually reaching the semi-finals of the competition.

But the drama of that first match, and the attention on it at a time when English clubs were banned from European football, means it will go down in Welsh footballing folklore.

The play has been written by local writer Anthony Bunko, and premiered on Thursday at the Coliseum theatre in Aberdare.

It was a dramatic game, with Merthyr's winner only coming in the 83rd minute thanks to a Ceri Williams free-kick deflecting off an Italian player, but Bunko believes the play is about much more than that.

"It's a football story. But it's not so much of a football story. The football is right at the end. It's a bit like the Full Monty, where the dance is right at the end. And with this play, the football is right at the end."

The plot follows a boy called Decker, and his efforts to fulfil a promise to take his grandfather's ashes to the game, but it is also about the wider community.

"It's all about the characters and their struggles to overcome. You've got Italians who come over, who are quite apprehensive. You've got the committee, who have got to go from an amateur to professionals. You've got a bit of a love story in it, because the Italians come over and fall in love with a Merthyr girl."

On the night at least 8,000 supporters were crammed into Penydarren Park, but Bunko admits that although he lives in Merthyr, he wasn't one of them.

"I was playing rugby at the time, so it passed me by", he said.

"But the last couple of years, I've been going up to Penydarren Park, and they always end up talking about that game. And I see all the photos on the wall. And I just thought I'd love to do something about it."

"I'm a proud Merthyr boy anyway. And I just wanted to fetch that part. Because the town gets a big kicking off everybody and I just wanted to show the communal side of it and how good it is."

Ben Evans plays the part of Kevin Rogers, the only Merthyr-born player in the team that beat Atalanta, and the man who scored in the 38th minute to go 1-0 up.

With many of those players expected to be at the opening performance on Thursday, Evans says he is excited, despite the added pressure on the cast.

"It's such an honour. I've been very, very lucky to speak to the marvellous Kevin Rogers, who I said to him that I hope I didn't let him down. And he's such a nice guy," said Evans.

"It's very much a Welsh thing that I probably didn't get starstruck meeting Rowan Atkinson or Anthony Hopkins and Michael Sheen. I got more starstruck meeting Gareth Bale and Ryan Giggs and Kevin Rogers and Ceri Williams."

"So, there will be a few extra nerves maybe. And I hope that I do Kevin and all the players justice."

Evans agrees that the significance of sporting events goes far beyond the results on the pitch, emphasising their impact on communities.

He added: "I was only three in '87, but in Wales especially, we hold on to these historical moments. Being from West Wales, we still talk about when Llanelli beat the All Blacks and that was a long time ago," Evans said.

"When we first came into the rehearsal space, we spoke not even about the match, but about Merthyr in 1987 and the problems that were going on economically and how this night gave the town hope. And it's something to make you believe, isn't it?"

Director Neil Maidman attended the famous fixture at Penydarren Park.

"It was absolutely amazing. I was a sixth former at the time. It happened on 16 September. My 18th birthday was on 17 September, so I attended the match the night before," he said.

"Looking back on it, that week was so instrumental in my entire life. I started my first job a few days later and then I actually met my future wife a few days later."

"To be doing and directing this play about that time, it's quite surreal, really."

The independent production looked in jeopardy at one point, as director Neil Maidman and Bunko struggled to secure funding for the project, "which was disappointing", said Bunko.

It's a mirror image of the events of 1987, where club chairman John Reddy led a campaign to raise tens of thousands of pounds, with an army of volunteers working day and night to renovate the stadium, in order to ensure the match could be played in the town.

"We weren't going to put [the play] on, and then the community got together, from business people and volunteers and we got enough money to actually put it on", Bunko said.

"We could then pay the actors good money and we could get the props and the costumes and everything we want."

"But it just showed our little punk rock spirit, and we got money from somewhere else, and on Thursday night we're going to have 500 people in here [The Aberdare Coliseum], which will be a good experience."

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy jury risks mistrial on 7th day of deliberations after 2 deadlock notes
articles.summary: Read the latest developments on this story here.
articles.body: Read the latest developments on this story here. Lindsay Clancy’s defense team filed a motion to Judge William Sullivan on Friday asking that there be no more sidebars for the remainder of the triple-murder trial, and that all further proceedings be handled in open court. The motion was filed as jurors in the murder trial were about to head into their seventh day of deliberations at Plymouth Superior Court after proceedings ended Thursday with the defense calling for the removal of one juror. The jury submitted a question after the lunch break Thursday; while Sullivan did not read the note in court, it appeared to have to do with reasonable doubt. He instead repeated his instructions on the definition of reasonable doubt and said each juror was brought in individually and asked whether they could follow his instructions before they were sent back to continue deliberations. “They’ve said at this point that they can,” Sullivan said. “That was specifically addressed towards the specific question, and that’s what I’m doing.” Sullivan sent everyone home for the day around 4 p.m. Just after 9 a.m. Friday, Sullivan allowed both the defense and the prosecution to argue how they think the judge should proceed with the juror who was apparently causing a holdup for the jury. While Sullivan did not confirm, defense attorney Kevin Reddington referenced a second note that might have been issued to the judge on the same issue just before dismissal Thursday. The prosecution suggested there be no further questioning of the jury and that the judge send them to continue deliberations, saying the juror has “no indication of lack of impartiality or bias or extraneous influence, and no indication of inability to deliberate.” But Reddington disagreed, and argued that the juror appears to have a personal issue that is hindering them from being able to deliberate fairly, and that the juror should be replaced with an alternate. He even suggested the juror has been dishonest under oath. Sullivan declined to throw the juror out and said there is no need for a further inquiry of that juror, adding that “the discharge of a deliberating juror is a sensitive undertaking, fraught with potential error.” Reddington objected, and asked Sullivan to give the jurors a harsher reminder of the law, saying the judge’s reading of the reasonable doubt law on Thursday was “soft.” “What do you want me to do? Get a brass band?” Sullivan shot back angrily. “The fact that I perhaps didn’t give it my full inflection — I’m sorry about that. I’m not an actor. I’ve just given the instructions.” Jurors issued deadlock notes to Sullivan on Tuesday and Wednesday, prompting the judge to issue what’s known as the Tuey-Rodriguez instruction, stating that a verdict is “preferable.” He then sent the group of nine women and three men back to deliberate for a final time. Based on Massachusetts law, a judge can only send a jury back for deliberations twice before declaring a mistrial, unless jurors consent to further deliberations. If the jury returns with a third deadlock note, Sullivan will likely declare a mistrial. A question from the jury on Thursday afternoon prompted a sidebar with Sullivan and the attorneys — which appeared to upset Reddington. It was not immediately clear what was said during the private conversation, but Reddington appeared animated and waved papers aggressively during the discussion, according to two members of the NBC News team in court. Reddington then walked over to Clancy, who looked upset, and wheeled her over to be included in the conversation. After the jury was dismissed for the day, Reddington alleged in court that one juror “refuses to listen to the law that you have given him or her on reasonable doubt.” He suggested that the “soft” instructions from Sullivan were not sufficient, and called for the removal of that juror. Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague then argued that there was “no way to determine what the deliberations are.” She said she felt the judge’s actions in response to the note were appropriate. Sullivan declined to remove a juror. The motion filed Friday suggests the defense wants the judge to read out all further jury questions and notes in open court, rather than keeping them private in sidebar. On Thursday, Reddington told reporters, “I want the public to know what’s going on.” While Reddington has told reporters outside the court that he is ready for a retrial as early as next week should this one end with a hung jury, he clarified Thursday after court it was not the result he wanted. “Why would I want a mistrial? I kicked the s--- out of their case,” he said. Prosecutors, however, have not indicated whether they are interested in retrying the case should it end in a mistrial. The jury must decide whether Clancy is criminally responsible for killing her three children, Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months. She is accused of strangling each of them to death using exercise bands before she threw herself out of her second-story window in a suicide attempt that left her paralyzed from the waist down. Reddington has argued that Clancy was compelled to act on auditory hallucinations that commanded her to carry out the killings, a symptom of postpartum psychosis, which he said she was experiencing at the time. The prosecution, though, has said that Clancy was not in psychosis when she killed her children. They say she planned out their killings and was aware of what she was doing when she murdered them. They have been pushing for a first-degree murder conviction, which would carry a life sentence for Clancy. The jury can also convict Clancy of lesser charges — second-degree murder or manslaughter — or deem her not guilty due to lack of criminal responsibility.

The responsibility (of the Ram temple) has now come onto my shoulders,” Mishra told PTI Videos before leaving for Delhi after his two-day visit to Ayodhya.Mishra, who headed the Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor, was appointed the first CEO of the temple trust on Wednesday.The trust also appointed Govind Dev Giri as general secretary, Mahesh Bhagchandka as treasurer, and inducted Madan Mohan Pandey and Nirmala Yadav as trustees.First visit focused on understanding temple operationsDuring his first visit to Ayodhya as the trust's CEO, Mishra said his immediate focus was on familiarising himself with the functioning of the temple and the trust.“I have only been here for one day, so this was a preliminary introductory visit. I will come here again after two or three days,” he said.“This was an introductory visit, during which I got an introduction to the functioning of the temple. Gradually, as I learn more about it, we will formulate some plans,” he added.Mishra also said he would move forward with the guidance and cooperation of the trust once he had gained a better understanding of the entire system.He said, “Right now I am trying to learn about the entire system myself. Once I understand everything, I will take orders and guidance from the Trust. With the cooperation of our team, we will move forward.”During his visit, trust members briefed Mishra on its administrative and financial operations, including accounting procedures. He also held meetings with members and office-bearers and inquired about the functioning of both the trust and the temple.Selected after 5,585 applicationsThe 62-year-old retired as head of the Western Air Command on April 30. He was selected from a shortlist of three candidates after 5,585 applications were received for the post.Mishra has 39 years of experience in various branches of the Indian Air Force and has been awarded the Uttam Yuddh Seva Medal.He had earlier described himself as “the most fortunate person” to have been given vital responsibilities twice in his life, once to serve the nation and now to serve Lord Ram and his devotees.“I consider myself the most fortunate person today to have been given vital responsibilities twice in my life -- once for national service and now for the organisation and administration of Shri Ram's temple and for Shri Ram's devotees,” he had said.Administrative overhaul at Ram temple trustMishra's appointment comes amid a wider administrative overhaul by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust following the controversy over alleged embezzlement of temple donations, which led to the arrest of eight people and the resignation of Champat Rai as its general secretary.Sources said the restructuring is aimed at strengthening the trust's administrative and financial systems as the temple's operations expand.The trust is expected to frame standard operating procedures for the CEO in the coming days, detailing his duties and responsibilities.The CEO is expected to oversee the implementation of the trust's policies and day-to-day administrative functioning, while major policy decisions and key financial matters will remain with the trustees.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Trump's peace envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv - reports say
articles.summary: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have led President Donald Trump's efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war - but talks have stalled.
articles.body:
US negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will visit Russia and Ukraine this weekend, reports say, as efforts to end the war appear to be gathering pace.

The envoys will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday in Moscow, and then will hold talks with Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky on Sunday in Kyiv, Axios said, citing US officials.

Witkoff and Kushner have led US President Donald Trump's efforts to broker a peace deal, but a gulf remains between the two warring sides.

Earlier on Friday, Zelensky said a Russian drone hit the office of Ukraine's security chief Oleksandr Poklad in Kyiv. Poklad appears to be unharmed.

In a post on social media, Zelensky said he had ordered Poklad, who head the SBU security service, to respond "adequately" to the attack.

Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Russia multiple times, but the purported talks will be the first in Ukraine.

Zelensky said on Thursday that "tentative dates have been set" and the US envoys would be in Kyiv "in the coming days".

But Ukrainian lawmaker Oleksiy Honcharenko said the pair were expected in the Ukrainian capital on Sunday. He added that this would happen after their visit to Moscow on Saturday.

Russia's state news agency Tass said Witkoff and Kushner were "expected to arrive in Moscow and then to Kyiv... on 5-6 September", quoting a source.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov later told reporters: "I wouldn't announce anything, but when these contacts take place, we will inform you."

Meanwhile, Putin told an international economic forum on Thursday that "there are chances" a peace deal could be reached.

"First of all, Moscow and Kyiv must agree between themselves," he said.

But he showed no sign of backing down from his maximalist demands, which included more territorial concessions from Ukraine.

Kyiv and its European allies have repeatedly rejected Putin's terms saying they are tantamount to capitulation.

Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and currently controls about 20% of its territory.

articles.title: In 1972, Illinois used 246,000 cubic yards of coal fly ash beneath 7,500 feet of expressway; monitoring found no evidence of settlement, frost or capillary-rise problems
articles.summary: US News: More than five decades ago, civil engineers in northern Illinois carried out a major engineering experiment by using 246,000 cubic yards of coal fly a.
articles.body: More than five decades ago, civil engineers in northern Illinois carried out a major engineering experiment by using 246,000 cubic yards of coal fly ash beneath 7,500 feet of a major expressway embankment. The pioneering project, completed in 1972 near Waukegan along the US Route 41 corridor, was one of the earliest large-scale examples of recycling industrial waste for American highway construction. Long-term monitoring showed that the alternative fill performed very well, with no signs of structural settlement, frost heave or problems caused by rising groundwater. Detailed technical studies of the project were later published by the National Cooperative Highway Research Program in NCHRP Synthesis 199, titled Recycling and Use of Waste Materials and By-Products in Highway Construction. The Federal Highway Administration also included the project in its detailed user guidelines. The findings helped change how state transportation departments across North America viewed industrial byproducts. They showed that fine ash collected from coal-fired power plants could replace traditional soil and aggregate used as backfill.Engineering a major highway embankment with industrial wasteThe decision by Illinois transport authorities in the early 1970s to use fly ash on such a large scale addressed two major problems: the high cost of digging and transporting natural soil, and the growing amount of industrial waste produced by Midwestern power plants. Fly ash is the non-combustible mineral material left after pulverised coal is burned in power plant boilers. Its particles are very fine, light and mostly spherical. Engineers found that when properly compacted, fly ash could provide strong resistance to shearing while weighing less than common clay or sand fills. During construction near Waukegan in 1972, contractors placed and compacted the 246,000 cubic yards of fly ash in controlled layers to create the main core of the embankment beneath the 7,500-foot road section. To prevent erosion and stop wind from carrying away the material during construction, crews covered the fly ash core with a thick layer of natural soil along the side slopes and road base. Instruments were installed throughout the site to track how the artificial embankment responded to heavy traffic and the severe freeze-thaw cycles common in northern Illinois winters.Technical evaluations confirm long-term structural stabilityMonitoring over several years showed that the fly ash core performed as well as, or better than, traditional soil embankments. According to NCHRP Synthesis 199, published under the Transportation Research Board, inspections after construction found no detectable uneven settlement across the 7,500-foot section. The ash also had pozzolanic properties, meaning it could react with moisture and free lime over time to form cement-like bonds. This helped increase its strength as the embankment aged. Monitoring teams also found no signs of frost heave during severe winter freezes. They did not detect capillary water movement that could damage or weaken the asphalt pavement above. Research records kept by the Federal Highway Administration in document FHWA-RD-97-148 noted that the Waukegan project became an important model for state transportation departments in Delaware, Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. These states later created formal standards for using fly ash in structural fills during the late 1970s and 1980s.Environmental standards and legacy of ash recyclingAlthough the 1972 Illinois project showed that coal ash could work well as a construction material, later decades brought stricter rules for managing the environmental risks linked to combustion waste. Early projects mainly focused on structural performance, moisture and density, and shear strength. Modern highway construction guidelines from the Environmental Protection Agency and state environmental agencies require detailed groundwater studies, protective sealing layers and groundwater monitoring. These measures help prevent trace heavy metals in fly ash from entering nearby water sources. Despite stronger environmental controls, the engineering principles proven on the 7,500-foot road section near Waukegan remain relevant to infrastructure projects around the world. The successful 1972 project showed that industrial combustion waste, when properly engineered and protected, could provide a strong and long-lasting alternative to natural aggregates in major transport corridors.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2000, Europe detected this tiny North American bug for the first time; 25 years later it could threaten 30 million hectares of oak forest
articles.summary: Europe News: A tiny insect that was first detected in Europe just 25 years ago has spread across the continent with remarkable speed, raising concerns about the fu.
articles.body: A tiny insect that was first detected in Europe just 25 years ago has spread across the continent with remarkable speed, raising concerns about the future of vast oak forests. The ‘oak lace bug,’ a North American species barely a few millimetres long, was first recorded in northern Italy in 2000. Since then, it has reached 25 countries and found favourable conditions among Europe’s abundant oak trees. A new research published in the ‘Journal of Pest Science’ warns that the insect could potentially occupy up to ‘30 million hectares’ of oak forest in Europe. Its feeding can discolour entire tree canopies, reduce photosynthesis and weaken young oaks. Researchers also believe its long-term effects could extend beyond individual trees, potentially affecting acorn production, forest regeneration and the many species that depend on oak ecosystems. Yet Europe still lacks an effective, sustainable way to control it.How could a tiny North American bug put 30 million hectares of European oak forest at riskAccording to the study, the oak lace bug (Corythucha arcuata) is native to the eastern United States and southern Canada. Adults measure only about 3.1 millimetres long and have transparent, lace-like wings. Despite its small size, the insect has proved remarkably successful outside its native range. The research states that the species was first documented in northern Italy in 2000. By the end of 2024, it had spread across much of Europe, while a first record from Belarus followed in 2025. The researchers describe human activity as a major driver of its long-distance spread, noting that early signs of invasion are often found along roadsides and near railways.The insect's ability to use a wide range of host trees has also helped its expansion. The study found that nearly all Eurasian deciduous oak species can serve as hosts. In Europe alone, the researchers estimate that there are at least 35 million hectares of oak forests available to the insect, although the study suggests that around 30 million hectares could potentially be occupied.Europe's vast oak forests have become ideal habitat for the invasive bugThe oak lace bug feeds mainly on the undersides of leaves. Both adults and young insects suck nutrients from the foliage, leaving yellowish-grey patches on the upper surface. Heavy infestations can become strikingly visible. According to the study, entire oak canopies can be discoloured by late summer, with severe damage sometimes appearing as early as June. In some heavily affected areas, the damage has become extensive enough to be detected through remote sensing.The problem is not simply cosmetic. The study reports that heavy oak lace bug infestations in Europe have been linked to a 58.8% reduction in photosynthesis and a 21.7% reduction in transpiration, the process through which trees move water. Damaged leaves may also fall between one and two months earlier than usual. These effects do not necessarily mean that an individual tree will immediately die. However, the researchers warn that repeated infestations over several years could gradually weaken oak health, particularly when trees are already dealing with drought, other insects or disease.Could repeated feeding affect future generations of oak treesOne of the major questions concerns acorns and the natural regeneration of oak forests. Field observations in Croatia and Hungary found that oak stands experiencing repeated outbreaks had higher levels of early acorn drop and unusually small acorns. The researchers are careful not to present this as definitive proof that the oak lace bug was solely responsible. Drought and extreme heat can also affect acorn development, and some of the observations occurred during a major European heatwave. Even so, similar symptoms were later recorded in heavily infested forests under less severe drought conditions.The review also points to evidence that the insect may affect young trees. The study found that repeated attacks could reduce the growth of oak seedlings. This raises concerns about whether persistent infestations could make it harder for some oak forests to regenerate naturally. That possibility matters because oaks support a remarkably diverse range of wildlife. Hundreds of insect and mite species are associated with oak trees, meaning a widespread decline in tree health could affect much more than the trees themselves.European winters may not be enough to stop the oak bugCold weather might seem like a natural barrier to an insect originating in North America, but the study suggests that European winters have not prevented the oak lace bug from spreading. Researchers found that the insects can survive surprisingly cold conditions. During a colder-than-average Hungarian winter, more than 60% of surveyed adults survived. Laboratory work also showed that some individuals could withstand prolonged exposure to temperatures as low as -5°C with relatively low mortality. The research says that low winter temperatures are unlikely to halt the insect's expansion across its invaded European range. Climate conditions still influence where it can thrive, but modelling discussed in the study suggests that further colonisation remains possible under future climate scenarios.Finding a safe way to control the oak lace bug remains difficultSeveral insecticides have shown promising results in experiments, but the researchers argue that spraying chemicals across Europe's enormous oak forests would not be economically or environmentally realistic. Oaks support high biodiversity, making large-scale chemical treatment particularly risky. Native European predators and parasites have also been observed feeding on the invasive insect, but so far none has shown enough ability to control populations effectively in the wild.The study identifies one potentially promising option named ‘Erythmelus klopomor,’ a tiny egg parasite found in the oak lace bug's native range. Researchers believe it could offer a long-term biological control method, but further work is needed to understand its behaviour and ensure that introducing it would not create ecological problems. 25 years after its first European detection, the oak lace bug has therefore become a serious and still-growing concern. The research makes clear that its full long-term impact remains uncertain, but the combination of rapid spread, widespread host trees and limited control options means the insect is unlikely to disappear from Europe's oak forests on its own.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Israel frees four more Lebanese prisoners in Red Cross-mediated handover
articles.summary: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun praises the release and thanks US President Donald Trump for his efforts.
articles.body:
Four Lebanese citizens who were held in Israel have been released and handed over to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the day after a first prisoner was freed.

In a statement on Friday, Lebanon’s President Joseph Aoun thanked the United States after the Red Cross facilitated the transfer. The US has been brokering talks between Beirut and Tel Aviv aimed at ending hostilities between the neighbouring countries.

Aoun expressed his gratitude “for all the efforts exerted, particularly by the US under the leadership of President Donald Trump and by international bodies, especially the ICRC”.

The ICRC confirmed that “at the request of the relevant parties, [it] facilitated the transfer to Lebanon of five individuals released from Israeli detention”.

Associated Press and Anadolu news agency reporters said they saw a convoy of ICRC vehicles heading towards the Naqoura border crossing on Friday morning and later returning. The convoy then entered a Lebanese army barracks in Tyre.

The release follows a pledge by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday that authorities would free five Lebanese prisoners.

The prisoner released on Thursday was identified as Malek Ghazi.

It was the first such handover since the outbreak of the latest Israel-Hezbollah war six months ago.

Other released prisoners include Hussein Ayash from the village of Harouf and Mohammed Juheir, a fisherman from the border town of Naqoura, AP reported.

Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres, including civilians as well as Hezbollah members captured during fighting in southern Lebanon.

The ICRC called for its teams to be granted access to the remaining prisoners unjustly held by Israel, noting that it has not had access to detainees held in Israel since October 2023.

“Many families in Lebanon are still waiting for answers about the fate of loved ones who may be detained, deceased or otherwise unaccounted for,” it said.

Clashes between the Israeli army and Hezbollah began after Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023. That led to over a year of hostilities that escalated into a full-blown war in 2024.

Two years later, Lebanon was fully drawn into the conflict when the US and Israel launched a war on Iran. Hezbollah, a key ally of Iran, fired rockets into Israel in retaliation for the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. Israel responded with air strikes and a ground invasion that have killed at least 4,300 people in Lebanon.

Lebanon began direct talks with Israel in April. Aoun’s government has vowed to fulfil the terms of the US-brokered framework agreement .

He said it would pave the way for “the full restoration of Lebanese sovereignty, without giving up an inch of our land or a single one of our people”.
